newsitem.title: USA: Hartford Whalers finalize move to North Carolina.
newsitem.headline: Hartford Whalers finalize move to North Carolina.

text.p: The National Hockey League's Hartford Whalers will move to Raleigh, N.C., and change their name to the Carolina Hurricanes, the team said in a statement late Tuesday.
The team said it has reached a 20-year lease agreement with city officials for a $120-million arena in Raleigh, to be ready for the 1999-2000 season.
The Whalers have an understanding with officials of the 21,500-seat Greensboro Coliseum for one or two years before the new arena is ready.
It is still not clear where the Whalers will play the 1997-98 season. They are contractually bound to Hartford until a $20.5 million exit agreement is signed.
The exit agreement was negotiated in late March between team owner Peter Karmanos and Connecticut Gov. John Rowland, a Republican.
The Connecticut Development Authority will meet Wednesday afternoon to discuss the exit agreement.

"The governor thinks this has gone on long enough," Rowland's spokesman, Dean Pagani, was quoted in the Hartford Courant as saying on Wednesday. "There is no reason to think we could get more than $20.5 million."

Connecticut House Speaker Tom Ritter, a Democrat, has been critical of the exit agreement and said Karmanos should be forced to pay at least $40 million for breaking his leave with the development authority.
The Whalers, Connecticut's only major league sports franchise, had been in Hartford since 1975. They contributed about $73 million a year to the capital city's economy.

Hartford Mayor Mike Peters said the city wants to make sure it is compensated fairly for the loss of the team, and that it might consider suing the development authority or the Whalers, the Courant reported.
